subject: hep-th
title_original: Krakow Lectures on Scalar Quantum Solitons
abstract: We give a pedagogical introduction to Linearized Soliton Perturbation Theory (LSPT), a new and efficient tool for calculations involving quantum solitons. It is a Hamiltonian approach with a focus on explicitly constructing the soliton states. These states are squeezed, coherent states plus perturbative corrections. We will describe multi-loop corrections to states and their masses. An inner product suitable for non-normalizable momentum eigenstates will be introduced and applied to kink-meson scattering. We will also discuss domain wall solitons.
title_relatable: A new way to calculate quantum solitons from the ground up
hook: A Hamiltonian approach for computing quantum soliton states and their properties through systematic perturbation theory.
summary: Linearized Soliton Perturbation Theory (LSPT) provides a direct method for constructing quantum soliton states as squeezed coherent states plus corrections, enabling multi-loop calculations of masses and scattering amplitudes. The framework handles non-normalizable momentum eigenstates and applies to kinks and domain walls. This pedagogical treatment makes an underused computational tool more accessible to researchers working with solitons in quantum field theory.
